item.title: Module: MYSQL
item.description:
MySQL is a widely used open-source relational database. Pigsty’s MYSQL module installs a fixed native MySQL 8.4 LTS platform on managed nodes. Choose a standalone instance or three-node single-primary InnoDB Cluster with Group Replication. The module manages TLS, backups, monitoring, and lifecycle.

Current status: Pilot module

MYSQL is a supplementary pilot module for a simple, low-cost MySQL cluster. Its scope is smaller than PGSQL. Deployment, convergence, HA failover, daily backups, monitoring, and alerts have systematic tests. Destructive complete-outage recovery and physical restore remain manual. Follow the Administration procedures.

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
Declare the cluster in inventory. mysql.yml adjusts live state to match. This page covers topology and configuration blocks. See Parameters for the full reference.

Before You Deploy

  • Manage nodes with NODE. Install the shared CA at /etc/pki/ca.crt through node_ca. MYSQL issues leaf certificates only.
  • Include mysql in repositories with node_repo_modules: node,infra,mysql, or cache packages locally with repo_extra_packages: [mysql].
  • Use supported platforms: x86_64 EL 8/9/10, Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 22/24; or aarch64 EL 9/10.
  • Set production mysql_root_password, mysql_monitor_password, and mysql_cluster_password. Preflight rejects CHANGE_ME placeholders.

item.title: Parameters
item.description:
Deployment exposes 11 parameters; removal adds two protected-operation parameters. Versions, ports, directories, charset, TLS paths, and schedules are fixed. Memory sizing follows node specifications. Use mysql_parameters to change server behavior.

Quick Reference

Parameter Level Default Description
mysql_cluster Cluster required Cluster name and identity
mysql_seq Instance required 1 for standalone; sequential 1..3 for HA
mysql_root_password Cluster DBUser.Root Local root password
mysql_monitor_password Cluster DBUser.Monitor Exporter identity password
mysql_cluster_password Cluster DBUser.Cluster AdminAPI/Router/backup identity password
mysql_databases Cluster [] Additive database declarations
mysql_users Cluster [] Additive user and grant declarations
mysql_parameters Cluster/Instance {} [mysqld] option overrides
mysql_backup_enabled Cluster true Daily full-backup timer
mysql_backup_repo Cluster see below Local backup path and retention
mysql_exporter_enabled Cluster true Exporter and monitoring target

The removal parameters are used by mysql-rm.yml:

item.title: Administration
item.description:
Declare state in the inventory and apply it with the playbook. Most dropped members or AdminAPI drift recover after ./mysql.yml -l <cluster>. Member replacement, physical restore, and complete-outage recovery require the manual procedures below.

Quick Reference

Operation Command
Deploy / converge a cluster ./mysql.yml -l <cluster>
Preflight without changes ./mysql.yml -l <cluster> --check
Local root session mysql --defaults-extra-file=/etc/mysql/pigsty/root.cnf
Inspect MGR topology SELECT MEMBER_HOST,MEMBER_STATE,MEMBER_ROLE FROM performance_schema.replication_group_members;
AdminAPI status dba.getCluster().status() in mysqlsh
Trigger a backup systemctl start mysql-backup (in HA, only the primary runs it)
Retire a secondary ./mysql-rm.yml -l <IP> -e mysql_safeguard=false -e mysql_rm_confirm=<instance>
Retire a whole cluster ./mysql-rm.yml -l <cluster> -e mysql_safeguard=false -e mysql_rm_confirm=<cluster>

Status Checks

Run these commands as root on a cluster member. Only root can read /etc/mysql/pigsty/ credentials. Examples use EL service names. Debian/Ubuntu uses mysql, not mysqld.

item.title: Playbook
item.description:
mysql.yml deploys and adjusts clusters to declared state. Separate mysql-rm.yml retires members or clusters with safeguards. Before every removal, recheck the target, backups, and exact confirmation value.

mysql.yml

Selected clusters follow check → install → bootstrap → access → provision → backup → monitor:

./mysql.yml -l my-test --check # preflight: validate declarations against the live state
./mysql.yml -l my-test # converge one cluster (must select all members)
./mysql.yml # converge every MySQL cluster in the inventory

item.title: Monitoring
item.description:
MYSQL sends mysqld_exporter metrics to VictoriaMetrics and Journald/Vector error logs to VictoriaLogs. Grafana supplies five dashboards. vmalert loads 68 recording rules and 27 alerts.

Collection Architecture

Each node runs mysqld_exporter on 9104 with least-privilege dbuser_monitor@'127.0.0.1'. Deployment creates a discovery file on the INFRA node:

/infra/targets/mysql/<instance>.yml # e.g. my-test-1.yml

The VictoriaMetrics mysql job reads this directory. mysql_exporter_enabled: false empties the target list. Only mysql-rm.yml removes the file.

item.title: Metrics
item.description:
mysqld_exporter supplies raw mysql_ metrics. vmalert derives mysql:ins:* and mysql:cls:* metrics for dashboards and alerts. This page defines those metrics.

files/victoria/rules/mysql.yml provides 68 module recording rules, all listed here. mysql_exporter_up = up{job="mysql"} additionally comes from Infra’s shared liveness recording rules. These recorded metrics do not appear at the raw mysqld_exporter endpoint. mysql_up is the exporter’s database connection probe result.

Common Labels

Metrics carry job=mysql, cls, ins, ip, and topology (standalone or innodb_cluster). Instance-derived metrics retain all identity labels. Cluster metrics aggregate to cls and topology.

item.title: FAQ
item.description:
How mature is the MYSQL module?

This pilot targets simple, low-cost MySQL clusters. Deployment/convergence, HA failover, daily backups, and monitoring/alerts have systematic tests, including fault injection and complete-outage exercises. Destructive recovery remains manual, with procedures. It has no PITR, VIP/DNS access layer, or automatic scaling; its scope is smaller than PGSQL. Before production, validate your requirements and rehearse recovery.

Why is MySQL fixed at 8.4? Can I pick a version?

The fixed platform pins server, client, Shell, Router, and XtraBackup to 8.4 LTS. This keeps compatibility predictable and avoids a broad version test matrix. That tradeoff keeps the pilot simple. Use another tool for other versions or extensive customization.
